name: b10c
cooked:
deadmanoz:

From the smaller size, something like warnet, up to simulating 10’s or 100’s of thousands of nodes.

I’ve worked on something that supports 10k-100k “nodes” recently to learn about address and block relay. Plan to post it to delving in a bit. There’s warnet, which runs a full node (using a real binary) and does real TCP transport, and there’s something like @mzumsande’s agent-based addrrelay_sim in Python, which does not use real Bitcoin Core source code, but implements the relay rules. Mine is somewhere between these. It’s based on Bitcoin Core source code, but does not run a full node and doesn’t do TCP connections by just passing around messages between different Bitcoin Core network managers.
